description: Deadline to file a Texas property tax protest with the appraisal review board: the later of May 15 or 30 days after the notice of appraised value was delivered, rolled past weekends and Texas legal holidays, plus a conservative file-by date (the last business day on or before the unadjusted deadline). status says where as_of (default: today in US Central time; echoed in as_of) falls: not_yet_open before January 1 of the tax year, open from then through the deadline, passed after it; days_remaining counts the days to the deadline (null once passed), and once passed next_season gives the same rule for the next tax year (May 15 basis). notes says what the rule does not cover (late protests, other §41.44 deadlines, §25.25 corrections) and which sections to read. Returns the statute citations, the rule's verification status and a disclaimer. Information about a statutory deadline: not legal or tax advice and not a substitute for the advice of an attorney. Verification status: verified. Cite rule rules.tx.property_tax_protest_deadline@2 and its statutes.

as_of.description: Date the status is measured from, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the current date in US Central time (America/Chicago), when the call is answered; pass it to fix the date (for a report, or for El Paso and Hudspeth counties, which keep Mountain time).

notice_delivered_date.description: Date the appraisal district's notice of appraised value was delivered (Tax Code §25.19), YYYY-MM-DD. A mailed notice is presumed delivered on the day it was deposited in the mail (§1.07(c)). Omit if unknown (May 15 is then the only basis).

name: rules_tx_property_tax_protest_deadline
title: Texas property tax protest deadline
